"Loudness equalization: pulls the overall loudness towards the target value, suitable for unifying the volume between different audios; threshold: limits the loudness to a range, more like automatic gain + suppression."
"Gradually pull the playback loudness towards the target value (the change is smoother and more suitable for unification between different audios). Recommended range: -24 to -14."
"When the volume is lower than this value, it will automatically amplify to close to the threshold."
"When the volume is higher than this value, it will be automatically suppressed to not exceed the threshold."
"Simulate common spaces or transmission media through band limiting, sound field narrowing, and delayed reflections. It is recommended to select a preset first and then fine-tune the intensity."
"The higher the intensity, the more obvious the scene features are. Presets such as phone sounds and bed muffled sounds will be more recognizable at high intensity."
"The bigger it is, the faster it plays (affecting the rhythm and duration)."
"The larger the pitch, the higher the pitch, and the smaller the pitch, the lower (not necessarily changing the playback duration)."
"The sound will be softer and slightly attenuated the further away it is."
"0° is centered, 90° is to the right, and 270° is to the left."
